title: Random forests nominate fungal taxa associated with leaf-warming samples
summary: An exploratory random forest identified three fungal sequence variants associated with warmed versus control leaf samples across six Florida plant species. Kondoa and Zasmidium candidates had lower mean counts in warmed samples, while a Cystobasidiomycetes variant had higher counts. Overall community richness and composition tests were null. These descriptive candidate associations do not establish differential abundance, causal taxon-specific warming effects or host-independent generalization.
ai_technology: Random forest; Boruta feature selection; naive Bayes taxonomy classifier
organization: University of Miami; University of Toronto; University of Waikato; North Carolina State University
